glance: Stocks closed the holiday-shortened week higher: S&P 500 +1.6%, Nasdaq +2.3% Friday as battered AI and memory-chip shares rebounded; the Dow had its best week since 2022.
Chip stocks bounced nearly 5% Friday but are still headed for their worst month since 2002 after November's AI selloff.
Nvidia reportedly told server partners to halt shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia under new US export rules.
The FCC authorized SpaceX to launch up to one million satellites for an orbital AI computing network.
Black Friday crowds hit stores after a record $82.5 billion in early-November online spending; OPEC+ meets Sunday amid Gulf tanker attacks.

tech.headline: Nvidia halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
tech.summary: Nvidia told partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping its AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia to comply with new US export controls, the Financial Times reported. The region has been a suspected transit route for advanced chips headed to China. It is the latest turn in a tumultuous month for Nvidia, whose board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday ahead of his congressional testimony next week.

tech.headline: SAP weighs at least 10,000 job cuts in AI restructuring
tech.summary: Europe's largest software company is preparing to eliminate roughly 9% of its workforce as it reorganizes around AI, according to Bloomberg. SAP said no decision has been made. The move would be one of the biggest AI-linked layoffs yet at a major enterprise software maker.

tech.headline: FCC clears SpaceX plan for a million AI-computing satellites
tech.summary: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for a proposed network that would run AI workloads in low Earth orbit on solar power. The approval covers a potential constellation, not satellites already built, and scientists have questioned the economics and how the hardware would shed heat. It signals regulators' willingness to let space-based data centers move ahead as AI power demand strains the grid.

tech.headline: Netherlands vows to fight US bill targeting ASML's China sales
tech.summary: The Dutch government says it will resist the proposed US Match Act, which would further restrict ASML's chipmaking-equipment sales to China, calling it a threat to the company. ASML's CEO separately argued that tighter controls would only speed up China's homegrown chip efforts.

tech.headline: Memory shortage pushes up electronics prices and dents phone sales
tech.summary: Some memory-chip prices have risen as much as tenfold in a year as AI data centers soak up supply, prompting companies to set up procurement war rooms, the WSJ reports. Counterpoint says US smartphone shipments fell 9% in the third quarter as costs squeezed Android makers, while Apple's share climbed to 57%.

tech.headline: OpenAI fixes GPT-6.2 billing error, will merge ChatGPT usage limits
tech.summary: OpenAI said a launch mistake with GPT-6.2 caused paying ChatGPT users to burn through usage allowances up to 40% faster, and that it has been corrected. Separately, the company plans to combine Chat and Work usage limits into one shared allowance, so heavy users of both may hit caps sooner; a wider rollout is planned for December.

tech.headline: Microsoft: Chinese and North Korean hackers adopt AI attack tool
tech.summary: Microsoft says state-backed groups from China and North Korea, including Salt Typhoon, have added the ARTEX AI penetration-testing tool to their arsenals. Separately, FIFA confirmed a breach exposing personal and business data, and Binance fully reopened withdrawals after last month's record $6.3 billion hack.

markets.asOf: market close, Nov 27 (early 12:00 PM CT close)
markets.summary: Stocks finished a volatile holiday week higher as AI and semiconductor shares rebounded on easing worries about AI profitability, though Treasury yields climbed after a strong GDP revision.

other.headline: Black Friday crowds return to stores after record online run-up
other.summary: Die-hard shoppers lined up at malls and big-box stores across the country Friday morning, even as online sales keep growing. Adobe says US consumers spent $82.5 billion online from Nov. 1 to 22, up 9.1% from a year ago, with higher electronics prices from the memory-chip shortage a wildcard for gift budgets.

other.headline: Trump calls for investigation after big GDP revision
other.summary: The government revised third-quarter growth up to 4.3% from 3.4%. President Trump alleged the initial figure was deliberately wrong and demanded an investigation; no probe has been confirmed.

other.headline: China and Japan push back on proposed US tariffs
other.summary: China rejected Washington's overcapacity rationale for new tariffs on 14 trading partners and said it reserves the right to respond, while Japan lodged a formal protest.

other.headline: Chinese stocks surge as Beijing steps in
other.summary: The Shanghai Composite jumped 4.2% and the CSI 300 rose 3.7% on Friday, their best days since October 2024, after the State Council called on state-backed investors to stabilize the market.

other.headline: Gulf tanker and refinery attacks keep oil on edge
other.summary: Oil rose more than $1 a barrel early Friday after new attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz and a Houthi strike claim on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, though rising US crude inventories tempered gains later. OPEC+ meets Sunday and is expected to hold output steady.
